claims.text: x402 is an open payment standard that uses the HTTP 402 Payment Required status code so a client can pay for a resource inside a normal request and response cycle.
The x402 repository describes the standard as aiming to support both crypto and fiat networks.
x402 originated at Coinbase Developer Platform.
The x402 whitepaper is dated 2025-05-06 and credits Erik Reppel, Ronnie Caspers, Kevin Leffew, Danny Organ, Dan Kim and Nemil Dalal.
The npm package x402 was created on 2025-02-20 and its version 0.3.0 was published on 2025-05-06, the public launch day.
Secondary coverage names AWS, Circle and Anthropic as x402 launch collaborators in May 2025, with one account adding NEAR and another naming the MCP project instead.
The Coinbase launch page for x402 could not be read (HTTP 403), so the launch partner list has no primary confirmation.
The GitHub repository x402-foundation/x402 was created on 2025-02-21 and is the original coinbase/x402 repository, transferred to the foundation organization.
The x402-foundation GitHub organization was created on 2026-04-01.
coinbase/x402 now exists on GitHub as a fork of x402-foundation/x402, created on 2026-04-02.
The x402-foundation organization holds repositories named tsc, wg-identity, wg-tax, wg-domain-discovery, wg-card-acceptance and foundation.
x402 is governed as x402 a Series of LF Projects, LLC, under a technical charter adopted on 2026-03-31.
The x402 technical charter sets up a Technical Steering Committee of representatives of participating organizations, with one vote per representative and decisions by majority.
The x402 charter requires a 75 percent supermajority vote to change the Core Principles or remove a participating organization, with a 10 business day voting window.
The charter PDF was added to the x402 repository by PR #1911, merged on 2026-04-02.
TSC.md lists the x402 Technical Steering Committee in seniority order as Coinbase (Erik Reppel), Cloudflare (Rohin Lohe) and Stripe (Steve Kaliski).
TSC.md was created by PR #2253, merged on 2026-05-12; the body is the Technical Steering Committee, not a generic steering committee.
On 2025-09-23 Cloudflare announced a plan to launch an x402 Foundation with Coinbase and proposed a deferred payment scheme.
On 2026-04-02 the Linux Foundation announced it was launching the x402 Foundation and welcoming the contribution of the x402 protocol, at MCP Dev Summit North America in New York.

The 2026-04-02 Linux Foundation release lists 22 organizations expressing intent or support, including Adyen, AWS, American Express, Circle, Cloudflare, Coinbase, Google, Mastercard, Microsoft, Shopify, Stripe and Visa.
The 2026-04-02 Linux Foundation release says the x402 standard was initially developed by Coinbase, Cloudflare and Stripe.
On 2026-07-14 the Linux Foundation announced the operational launch of the x402 Foundation and said 40 organizations had joined as members.

The x402 Foundation lists 17 Premier members: Adyen, AWS, American Express, Circle, Cloudflare, Coinbase, Fiserv, Google, Mastercard, Monad Foundation, MoonPay, Ripple, Shopify, Solana Foundation, Stellar Development Foundation, Stripe and Visa.
The x402 Foundation lists 18 General members, including Fireblocks, KakaoPay, Merit Systems, NEAR Foundation, Polygon Labs, World Liberty Financial and zerohash.

The x402 Foundation lists Associate members BSV Association, Cardano Foundation, Casper and Japan Contents Blockchain Initiative, and OMA3; the listed names total 39 or 40 depending on how the Casper entry is counted.
x402 code is licensed under Apache License 2.0 and the NOTICE file reads Copyright 2026 x402 Foundation.
No CC-BY license text for the x402 docs was found anywhere in the repository.
x402 CONTRIBUTING.md requires GPG signed commits rather than a DCO sign-off.
New x402 schemes need a spec PR under specs/schemes/ first, then one reference SDK implementation, then other SDKs.
The x402 docs at docs.x402.org describe themselves as a credibly neutral source of truth and ask contributors to keep them free of branded content.
The x402Version field takes the value 1 or 2, and version 2 is the current protocol.
The x402 v2 specification version table dates v2.0 to 2025-12-09 and summarizes it as CAIP-2 networks, restructured PaymentPayload and PaymentRequired, ResourceInfo separation and extension support.
The x402 specification version tables date v0.1 to 2025-08-29 and v0.2, a transport-agnostic redesign, to 2025-10-03.
x402 V2 launched on 2025-12-11, when PR #705 Development v2 merged and @x402/core 2.0.0 was published to npm.
The x402 V2 launch post claims over 100M payments were processed before V2 and says the SDKs remain backward compatible with V1.
The V1 x402 specification is kept in the repository alongside the V2 specification.
Every @x402 npm package in the repository is at version 2.28.0, and @x402/core 2.28.0 was published to npm on 2026-09-29.
@x402/core has shipped minor releases roughly weekly, for example 2.1.0 on 2025-12-23, 2.9.0 on 2026-04-02 and 2.23.0 on 2026-08-18.
Only the npm packages x402 and x402-express are V1 legacy x402 packages; the @x402 scoped packages implement V2.
The npm package x402 has latest version 1.2.0, published on 2026-04-16.
The PyPI package x402 is the V2 Python SDK, not a legacy V1 package, with latest version 2.25.0 published on 2026-09-29.
PyPI x402 1.0.0 was released on 2025-12-10 and 2.0.0 on 2026-01-22, with 36 releases in total.
The Go SDK module is github.com/x402-foundation/x402/go/v2, requiring Go 1.24, with a v2.28.0 changelog entry dated 2026-09-29.
The Java x402 module in the repository is version 1.0.0-SNAPSHOT with PaymentFilter, FacilitatorClient and X402HttpClient, and no published artifact was found.
The exact scheme EVM specification was first merged on 2025-02-23 in PR #1, before the public launch.
Permit2 support in the exact EVM scheme was merged on 2026-01-08 in PR #769.
The bazaar discovery extension specification was first merged on 2026-01-15 in PR #956.
The sign-in-with-x extension specification, based on CAIP-122, was first merged on 2026-02-02 in PR #921.
The upto scheme specification was merged on 2026-03-04 in PR #1074.
The offer-receipt extension was first merged on 2026-03-12 in PR #935, and its own version table lists 0.5 as the first approved release on 2026-01-29.
The batch-settlement scheme, its cloudflare:402 binding and the http-message-signatures extension were merged on 2026-04-15 in PR #1145.
The builder-code extension, based on ERC-8021, was first merged on 2026-05-04 in PR #2050.
The batch-settlement EVM specification was first merged on 2026-05-05 in PR #2051, and its version table date of 2025-04-28 appears to be a typo for 2026.
The auth-capture scheme specification was merged on 2026-05-13 in PR #1425, not on 2026-05-12, and v1.1 followed in PR #3197 merged 2026-08-25.
The exact scheme on Lightning (lnbtc) was specified in PR #2861, Specify exact Lightning on BIP-122, merged on 2026-09-23.
x402's deferred scheme was renamed batch-settlement: Cloudflare proposed deferred in 2025-09, and PR #1145 introduced batch-settlement while unifying the deferred-settlement PRs.
PR #426, which proposed a deferred payment scheme spec in 2025-09, was closed without merging on 2026-05-15.
Residue of the old deferred name survives in the auth-hints extension examples and in the V1 specification's list of example schemes.
@x402/core 2.23.0, published 2026-08-18, added client spendControls with a default cap of $1 per payment, SIWX origin binding and settleOnCancel.
@x402/core 2.21.0 added Cache-Control no-store on 402 responses and fixed a wildcard route payment bypass via percent-encoded line terminators.
@x402/core 2.22.0 fixed a paywall bypass via a backslash in path parameters, and 2.27.0 matches routes against both escaped and decoded paths.
@x402/core 2.26.0 added extra.minDeposit for batch-settlement with a default of 10 times the amount.
x402 defines three main roles: a client that wants to pay for a resource, a resource server that provides it, and a facilitator that verifies and executes payments for one or more networks.
The x402 docs state that the facilitator does not hold funds or act as a custodian.
Anyone can run an x402 facilitator, and a resource server can verify and settle payments itself without a separate facilitator.
A trust-minimizing principle in the x402 README says no payment scheme may let the facilitator or resource server move funds other than in accordance with client intentions.
For Solana exact payments the fee payer that signs the transaction may be the merchant or a third-party facilitator, and is advertised in extra.feePayer.
In the cloudflare:402 credit-backed binding the network itself acts as merchant of record and payTo is the constant merchant.
The V2 PaymentRequired object has the fields x402Version, error, resource, accepts and extensions, of which x402Version, resource and accepts are required.
The V2 ResourceInfo object has the fields url (required), description, mimeType, serviceName, tags and iconUrl.
A V2 PaymentRequirements entry has the required fields scheme, network, amount, asset, payTo and maxTimeoutSeconds, plus an optional extra object.
In V2 PaymentRequirements the network field is a CAIP-2 identifier such as eip155:84532, and amount is a string in atomic units.
The extra object of PaymentRequirements reserves the keys assetTransferMethod and paymentFlow; other keys are scheme specific, such as name and version for the EVM token's EIP-712 domain.
Each x402 extension entry has an info object and a JSON Schema in schema, and clients must echo at least the received info back without deleting or overwriting it.
The V2 PaymentPayload object has the fields x402Version, resource, accepted, payload and extensions, where accepted is the chosen PaymentRequirements entry.
The exact EVM payload with the eip3009 method carries a signature and an authorization with from, to, value, validAfter, validBefore and nonce.

The exact EVM permit2 payload carries a permit2Authorization whose spender is the x402ExactPermit2Proxy at 0x402085c248EeA27D92E8b30b2C58ed07f9E20001, and the erc7710 payload carries delegationManager, permissionContext and delegator.
The Solana exact payload is a single transaction field holding a base64 partially signed versioned transaction.
The VerifyResponse object has the fields isValid (required), invalidReason, payer, extensions and extra.
The SettleResponse object, also called SettlementResponse in the spec headings, has the fields success, errorReason, payer, transaction, network, amount and extensions.
In SettleResponse the transaction field is an empty string if nothing was broadcast and must be non-empty when errorReason is settlement_pending.
The SupportedResponse from GET /supported has the fields kinds, extensions and signers, where signers maps CAIP-2 patterns to signer addresses.

A discovery resource returned by GET /discovery/resources has the fields resource, type, x402Version, accepts, lastUpdated and extensions, and the list takes limit values from 1 to 100 with a default of 20.

V1 PaymentRequirements used the fields scheme, network, maxAmountRequired, asset, payTo, resource, description, mimeType, outputSchema, maxTimeoutSeconds and extra, with networks as plain strings such as base-sepolia.

The bazaar extension describes inputs with info.input.type of http or mcp, plus method, queryParams, bodyType, body, headers, toolName and inputSchema, and outputs with info.output.type and info.output.example.
The payment-identifier extension carries info.required and info.id, an identifier of 16 to 128 characters.
The offer-receipt extension carries signed offers with format eip712 or jws, payload, signature and acceptIndex, using EIP-712 domains named x402 offer and x402 receipt.
The sign-in-with-x extension sends a SIGN-IN-WITH-X client header and its info includes domain, uri, version, nonce, issuedAt, expirationTime, statement and resources.
The builder-code extension appends an ERC-8021 Schema 2 CBOR suffix to settlement calldata with keys a for app, w for wallet or facilitator, s for service and m for facilitator metadata.
The auth-hints extension lists authRequirements with acceptIndexes and methods that name type, tokenType and authorizationServer.

The x402 extension identifiers in the specs are bazaar, sign-in-with-x, payment-identifier, offer-receipt, builder-code, http-message-signatures, auth-hints, eip2612GasSponsoring and erc20ApprovalGasSponsoring.
x402 V2 defines four schemes: exact, upto, batch-settlement and auth-capture.
In the V2 HTTP flow the resource server answers an unpaid request with status 402 and a PAYMENT-REQUIRED header holding base64 encoded PaymentRequired JSON.
In the V2 HTTP flow the client retries the same request with a PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header holding a base64 encoded PaymentPayload.
In the default authorization flow the resource server calls the facilitator's POST /verify, runs the handler only if the payment is valid, then calls POST /settle.
The facilitator /verify and /settle request body contains x402Version, paymentPayload and paymentRequirements.
After settlement the server returns 200 with the resource and a PAYMENT-RESPONSE header holding a base64 encoded SettleResponse, or 402 with PAYMENT-RESPONSE carrying success false.
V2 HTTP header names differ from V1: V1 used a JSON body for requirements and the headers X-PAYMENT and X-PAYMENT-RESPONSE, while V2 uses PAYMENT-REQUIRED, PAYMENT-SIGNATURE and PAYMENT-RESPONSE.
x402 V2 defines three payment flows in extra.paymentFlow: authorization (verify, execute, settle), upfront (settle before the resource) and escrow (settle, execute, settle).
The x402 V2 spec requires that at least one verify or settle call runs before the resource executes, and /verify must not write state.
Clients must not build a payment for an unrecognized payment flow and should prefer authorization when several flows are offered.

The exact scheme on Lightning uses the upfront flow: the server issues a fresh BOLT11 invoice in extra.invoice, the client returns the preimage, and the facilitator checks the hash and records it in a replay store.
The auth-capture scheme defaults to the escrow flow, where a first settle places a hold, the resource runs and a second settle captures the actual amount or voids the hold.
In the EVM upto scheme the client signs a Permit2 authorization for a ceiling amount and the server settles the metered charge, which must not exceed the ceiling; a zero charge needs no transaction.
The EVM upto scheme returns 412 Precondition Failed with the code PERMIT2_ALLOWANCE_REQUIRED when the Permit2 allowance is missing.
The batch-settlement EVM scheme opens a payment channel with a deposit, carries a cumulative voucher on each request and later claims and settles many vouchers in one token transfer.
In batch-settlement EVM a client can leave a channel with initiateWithdraw and then finalizeWithdraw after a withdrawDelay of 15 minutes to 30 days.

In the cloudflare:402 binding the client signs each request with RFC 9421 headers Signature-Agent, Signature-Input and Signature, sends amount and asset in PAYMENT-SIGNATURE with asset USD, and Cloudflare bills the identity later.
The cloudflare:402 binding defines error codes blocked, price_not_acceptable, payment_failed, invalid_signature, signature_agent_unknown, invalid_payment_signature, origin_error and unknown.
Exact EVM verification failures include insufficient_funds, invalid_exact_evm_payload_signature, invalid_network, invalid_scheme, unsupported_scheme and invalid_x402_version.
A settle timeout is indeterminate in x402: settlement may still have happened, and settlement_pending is a non-terminal result that the server retries once and reconciles.
The V2 HTTP transport uses status 402 for payment required, 400 for an invalid payment, 402 for a failed payment, 500 for a server error and 200 for success.
The A2A transport uses the x402.payment.status values payment-required, payment-rejected, payment-submitted, payment-verified, payment-completed and payment-failed.
The auth-capture scheme defines the operations authorize, charge, capture, void, refund and reclaim, where reclaim is client only after extra.captureDeadline.
Batch-settlement channel contracts emit ChannelCreated, Deposited, Claimed, Settled, Refunded, WithdrawInitiated, WithdrawFinalized and ChannelClosed events.

In the MCP transport an unpaid tool call returns a result with isError true and PaymentRequired in structuredContent, the client retries with _meta x402/payment, and the server returns _meta x402/payment-response.
In the A2A transport the agent puts the task in input-required with x402.payment.required metadata, and the client answers with x402.payment.payload; receipts return in x402.payment.receipts.
The x402 A2A transport spec uses the extension URI https://github.com/google-a2a/a2a-x402/v0.1, while a2a-x402 v0.2 uses https://github.com/google-agentic-commerce/a2a-x402/blob/main/spec/v0.2.
Facilitator APIs are HTTP in every x402 transport: POST /verify, POST /settle, GET /supported, GET /discovery/resources and GET /discovery/search.
Cloudflare AI Gateway accepts a PAYMENT-METHOD: x402 header to pay for inference with x402 instead of the account's billing method.
Every x402 EVM signature uses EIP-712 typed data, and exact with eip3009 signs TransferWithAuthorization(address from,address to,uint256 value,uint256 validAfter,uint256 validBefore,bytes32 nonce).
x402 uses EIP-3009, EIP-2612, Uniswap Permit2, ERC-7710 delegations, ERC-1271 and ERC-6492 smart wallet signatures, and ERC-8021 builder codes on EVM chains.
x402 network identifiers are CAIP-2 strings such as eip155:8453 and stellar:pubnet; ach:us and sepa:eu appear only as examples of the encouraged format for non-blockchain rails.
The cloudflare:402 binding and the http-message-signatures extension use RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signatures with Ed25519 and key directories at /.well-known/http-message-signatures-directory.
The x402ExactPermit2Proxy and x402UptoPermit2Proxy contracts are deployed with CREATE2 at the same address on every supported EVM chain.
In exact EVM payments the client signature covers the recipient and the amount, so the facilitator can broadcast the transaction but cannot change the amount or destination.
x402 replay protection relies on a 32 byte random nonce that EIP-3009 token contracts refuse to reuse, plus validAfter and validBefore time windows.
The EVM upto scheme adds witness.facilitator so that only the announced facilitator can settle the payment.
The exact scheme defines no refund, and any remedy is the resource server's own arrangement.
Refunds exist in x402 only in auth-capture (void, refund, reclaim), in batch-settlement channels, or through third parties such as x402r.
The upto scheme requires clients to trust servers to charge fairly up to the ceiling, and the upfront flow leaves a client charged if the handler fails.

GitHub advisory GHSA-3j63-5h8p-gf7c, published 2025-08-20 with high severity, affects the npm packages x402, x402-next, x402-express and x402-hono below 0.5.2 and mainly impacts resource server builders.
GitHub advisory GHSA-qr2g-p6q7-w82m, published 2026-03-07 with high severity, affects facilitators processing Solana payments and is patched in @x402/svm 2.6.0, PyPI x402 2.3.0 and Go 2.5.0.
Neither x402 GitHub advisory has a CVE identifier.
The x402 repository ships three Cantina audit reports for the EVM contracts, dated February, March and May 2026.
The x402 SECURITY.md still routes vulnerability reports to Coinbase's HackerOne program.
The x402 Solana SDK blocks duplicate settlement submissions with a 120 second in-memory SettlementCache.

arXiv:2605.11781, Five Attacks on x402 Agentic Payment Protocol (2026-05-12), presents five practical attacks on authorization, binding, replay protection and web-layer handling and audits three open source SDKs.
arXiv:2607.19545, When HTTP 402 Meets the Blockchain (2026-07-21), studies facilitator-mediated deployments, proposes eight security rules for facilitators and reports four new attack vectors.
The claim that all 15 tested facilitators violated at least one rule in arXiv:2607.19545 is not visible in the paper's abstract.
arXiv:2605.30998, Free-Riding the Agentic Web (2026-05-29), describes four flaw classes in x402 including cross-resource substitution and a duplicate settlement race.
arXiv:2603.01179, A402 (2026-03-01), argues x402 does not make execution, payment and delivery atomic and proposes Atomic Service Channels.
arXiv:2604.11430, Hardening x402 (2026-04-13), treats resource metadata sent to servers and facilitators as a PII leakage channel and proposes redacting middleware.
arXiv:2609.00060, A Formal Analysis of Agent Payment Protocols (2026-08-30), builds Tamarin models of x402, MPP, ACP and AP2.
The x402 TypeScript client applies spendControls by default: only default assets and at most $1 per payment, set by DEFAULT_MAX_AMOUNT_PER_PAYMENT in x402Client.ts.
Passing spendControls false disables the x402 client spending limits, which the browser paywall does because a human approves in the UI.
Client-side budget management is out of scope for the x402 protocol, so spending budgets exist only in SDKs and wallets.
Time-bound authorization in x402 comes from validAfter, validBefore, deadline, maxTimeoutSeconds and invoice expiry.
The payment-identifier extension provides idempotency, and a server returns 409 when the same identifier arrives with a different payload fingerprint.
x402 has no dispute process in the protocol.
The offer-receipt extension provides signed offers and receipts, but per the SDK parity table it is implemented in TypeScript only.
Identity in x402 is optional and separate from payment, provided by sign-in-with-x, auth-hints (OAuth 2.0 with DPoP) and RFC 9421 agent signatures for cloudflare:402.
x402 has no sanctions or KYT layer in the protocol; the CDP facilitator runs OFAC and Know Your Transaction checks on payments.
The builder-code extension provides on-chain attribution but not revenue sharing; affiliate splits come from the third-party x402aff package.

The x402 SDKs expose lifecycle hooks such as onBeforeVerify, onAfterVerify, onBeforeSettle, onAfterSettle and onVerifiedPaymentCanceled, plus client hooks onBeforePaymentCreation and onPaymentRequired.
An exact eip3009 payment appears on chain only as the token's own Transfer and AuthorizationUsed events, so nothing marks it as an x402 payment.

The canonical x402 EVM contract addresses are x402ExactPermit2Proxy 0x402085c248EeA27D92E8b30b2C58ed07f9E20001, x402UptoPermit2Proxy 0x4020A4f3b7b90ccA423B9fabCc0CE57C6C240002 and x402BatchSettlement 0x4020074e9dF2ce1deE5A9C1b5c3f541D02a10003.
The x402 contracts README lists batch settlement as deployed on Base, Arbitrum, World Chain, Polygon, Optimism, Avalanche, Celo, Linea, Unichain and Monad mainnets.

The public x402.org facilitator is testnet only and its GET /supported listed exact, upto and batch-settlement on eip155:84532 plus exact on Solana devnet, Algorand testnet, aptos:2, stellar:testnet, hedera:testnet and xrpl:1.
The CDP Bazaar discovery endpoint at api.cdp.coinbase.com/platform/v2/x402/discovery/resources answered without an API key, and the CDP docs say Bazaar discovery is public.
The Bazaar discovery API returns resource listings, not category data, so x402 resource categories should not be claimed unless the API returns them.
x402scan is an x402 explorer and registry operated by Merit Systems, with public API routes for buyers, facilitators, merchants, origins, registry, resources, send and wallets.
x402scan's discovery document checks /openapi.json with x-payment-info first, then /.well-known/x402, and treats runtime 402 behavior as authoritative over static metadata.
The x402scan README shows an Apache 2.0 badge but the repository has no LICENSE file and GitHub reports no license.
x402 header contents, including resource URLs, descriptions and amounts, travel only between client, server and facilitator, and batch-settlement vouchers stay in server storage until claimed.
Credit-backed cloudflare:402 commitments never reach a chain, and the mapping from signature identity to billing account is held by Cloudflare.
The x402 protocol has no built-in KYC, know-your-agent or sanctions layer, and compliance is left to facilitators.
Fiat and credit rails appear in the x402 spec through ISO 4217 asset codes and the cloudflare:402 binding, where Cloudflare is merchant of record with its own billing and dispute terms.
The x402 charter allows removal of a representative or participating organization if a regulator with jurisdiction over the project directs it.
The Cloudflare Monetization Gateway closed beta is limited to eligible US-based sellers and buyers.
Stripe's x402 machine payments preview was reported as available to US businesses only and as mapping settlements onto PaymentIntents.
The x402 Foundation has a wg-tax working group repository, but no x402 tax specification content exists yet.

The official x402 npm packages include @x402/core, @x402/evm, @x402/svm, @x402/fetch, @x402/axios, @x402/express, @x402/hono, @x402/next, @x402/fastify, @x402/paywall, @x402/extensions and @x402/mcp, plus network packages such as @x402/stellar and @x402/near.
The PyPI x402 package offers the extras httpx, requests, fastapi, flask and svm.
SDK parity is uneven: TypeScript covers 13 network families, Go covers evm and svm, and Python covers evm, svm and tvm without auth-capture or SVM batch-settlement.
The x402 docs list third-party SDKs Mogami (Java), x402-rs (Rust) and x402-rails (Ruby), and third-party extensions including x402r for refunds and arbitration.
The x402 docs list facilitators including CDP, PayAI, Corbits, Dexter, Fireblocks, Polygon, Celo, NEAR x402 Facilitator and T54 XRPL, and say the list is not exhaustive.
Default dollar-priced assets in x402 are mostly USDC, but defaults also include USDT0 on Stable, MegaUSD on MegaETH, USDM on Cardano and USDT on TON, so not every x402 payment is USDC on Base.
The CDP facilitator supports Base, Base Sepolia, Polygon, Arbitrum, World and World Sepolia for exact, upto and batch-settlement, and Solana mainnet and devnet for exact and upto.
Coinbase Agentic Wallets, announced on 2026-02-11, were reported to transact through x402.
Stripe launched a machine payments preview on 2026-02-10 that charges agents in USDC on Base through x402.
Circle Nanopayments powered by Circle Gateway went live on mainnet on 2026-04-29, using EIP-3009 authorizations inside the x402 flow with batched settlement.
The Cloudflare Monetization Gateway closed beta of 2026-09-30 settles USDC on Base through Coinbase's x402 facilitator.
The credit-backed cloudflare:402 network with RFC 9421 signatures is a separate batch-settlement variant, not the settlement path of the Monetization Gateway beta.
Cloudflare's Agents SDK has supported x402 for agents and MCP servers through withX402 and paidTool since 2025-09-23.
The CDP x402 facilitator makes the first 1,000 on-chain facilitator transactions each month free and charges $0.001 per on-chain transaction after that, while verification is always free.
On the CDP facilitator, exact and EVM upto settle in one on-chain transaction per payment, Solana upto needs two, and batch-settlement claims many vouchers in one transaction.

A secondary comparison reports PayAI charging $0.001 per settlement after 1,000 free settlements and thirdweb charging a 0.3 percent facilitator fee; self-hosted facilitators pay only gas and operations.
Under normal congestion a USDC transfer costs about $0.005 to $0.01 on Base, $0.001 to $0.005 on Solana and $1 to $5 on Ethereum L1, by a secondary mid-2026 estimate.
Circle Nanopayments accepts payments from $0.000001 USDC with off-chain authorizations at zero gas and publishes no per-transaction fee schedule.
In x402 the facilitator usually pays gas: it co-signs as fee payer on Solana and broadcasts EIP-3009 or Permit2 settlements on EVM chains.
The x402-foundation/x402 repository had 6,701 stars, 2,158 forks and 693 open issues.
Over the last 30 days npm recorded 1,492,519 downloads of @x402/core and 2,007,353 downloads of the legacy x402 package, figures that include CI installs.
The x402.org Last 30 Days counters showed 75.41M transactions, $24.24M volume, 94.06K buyers and 22K sellers, with the page saying Last updated: 2026-08-25.
Crypto Briefing reported the same $24.24M 30 day x402 volume figure for mid August 2026, so the x402.org counter appears unchanged since at least then.
The claim that the x402.org counter has been static since March 2026 could not be verified.
The CDP docs claim over 100 million x402 payments across Base and Solana.
Visa and Artemis data to 2026-04-21 adjusts x402 activity to about $15.0M across 109.6M transactions, an average of $0.14, against unadjusted $135.7M and 178.3M operations.
Visa's Cuy Sheffield separately cited about $19M across about 134M adjusted x402 transactions, a figure that conflicts with the roughly $15M in the Visa and Artemis chart.
The top 1 percent of x402 buyers, about 4,000 wallets, drove about 90 percent of adjusted volume in Visa and Artemis data.
Artemis flagged on average 63.94 percent of x402 transactions as gamed between 2025-11-09 and 2026-02-07, with a peak of 90.21 percent.
The Linux Foundation said Solana carried nearly 65 percent of x402 transaction volume in 2026 up to 2026-04-02.

Solana was reported at about 70 percent of monthly x402 volume in mid August 2026, and to have passed Base in daily transactions on 2026-08-25, while Base held about 90 percent of adjusted transactions in Visa and Artemis data.
Cumulative x402 transaction counts were reported between 120 million and 187 million depending on the tracker.
arXiv:2607.12575 counts 136,708,672 x402 settlements on Base over a 280 day window and argues the count is not evidence of adoption because settlement counts can be manufactured almost for free.
x402 volume figures are contested: raw counters, adjusted Visa and Artemis totals and academic measurements disagree by an order of magnitude.
Daily x402 transactions surged during the PING memecoin launch in late October 2025, with nearly 500,000 transactions in the week of 2025-10-14 to 2025-10-20.
The figures of about $1.59M in three days and 74,000 buyers by 2025-10-26 during the PING spike could not be re-located in a source.
The seed estimate that 25 to 30 percent of x402 activity is leaderboard farming has no located source.
Google's AP2 announcement of 2025-09-16 launched the A2A x402 extension with Coinbase as a way to use x402 payments with AP2.
The a2a-x402 v0.2 Embedded Flow places x402 payment requirements inside an AP2 v0.1 CartMandate and the PaymentPayload inside a PaymentMandate; AP2 v0.2 has no Cart mandate.
The AP2 repository ships human-present/x402 and human-not-present/x402 samples and an x402_psp_mcp role.
MPP's documentation says the x402 exact model maps onto MPP's charge intent and that mppx lets one server route accept either an MPP or an x402 credential.
Stripe is both a Premier member and TSC participant of the x402 Foundation and a co-creator of MPP.
The Visa Trusted Agent Protocol sample merchant backend returns 402 with non-standard X-Payment-Required, X-Payment-Session-ID and X-Payment-Amount headers, so it does not use the x402 wire format.
A browsingIOU object linking Visa TAP to HTTP 402 was not found in the cloned Visa TAP repository.
No mention of x402 was found in the cloned OpenAI ACP repository, and no mention of ACP in the x402 repository.
No mention of x402 was found in the cloned UCP repositories.
ERC-8004 treats payments as orthogonal but its registration file has an x402Support boolean, and its off-chain feedback file can carry a proofOfPayment for an x402 payment.
ERC-8004 best practices recommend agentWallet as the x402 receipt address and note that indexers cannot easily tell x402 payments from generic transfers.
Mastercard is a Premier member of the x402 Foundation, which has a wg-card-acceptance working group, but no x402 mention was found in the cloned Mastercard agent toolkit.
L402 is an earlier HTTP 402 payment design on Lightning by Lightning Labs; no source states that it is the ancestor of x402.
The original Lightning Labs L402 design used a macaroon and a BOLT11 invoice in WWW-Authenticate, while bLIP-0026 (2023-06-06) is token-agnostic and makes macaroons optional.
x402's lnbtc binding reuses the Lightning preimage proof but carries it in PAYMENT-SIGNATURE with no macaroon.
x402 is distinct from L402 (Lightning Labs), A402 (an academic proposal) and x402r (a third-party refund and arbitration protocol).
x402 was originated by Coinbase and is now governed under the Linux Foundation as the x402 Foundation, not by Coinbase alone.
x402scan is operated by Merit Systems, which publishes its source repository on GitHub.
Merit Systems is a General member of the x402 Foundation.
Facilitators may return extension data to the resource server through an EXTENSION-RESPONSES header sidechannel that is never forwarded to buyers.
The V1 PaymentPayload had the fields x402Version, scheme, network and payload, and the V1 SettlementResponse had success, errorReason, transaction, network and payer.
The A2A transport declares the x402 extension in AgentCard.capabilities.extensions and activates it with the X-A2A-Extensions header.
The x402 default facilitator URL in the SDK packages is https://x402.org/facilitator, which serves testnets only.
Critics note facilitator centralization: the protocol is permissionless, yet CDP processes most payments and Cloudflare's gateway also routes through Coinbase's facilitator.
Base64 JSON in x402 headers can exceed 2 KB and may be dropped by intermediaries, so the cloudflare:402 binding strips schema and optional fields.
The x402 specs show naming drift, including SettleResponse versus SettlementResponse and leftover deferred examples after the rename to batch-settlement.
The x402 Technical Steering Committee consists of three companies, and Stripe sits on both the x402 TSC and the MPP project.
x402 Foundation Premier membership was reported to cost $200,000.
The a2a-x402 repository declares a Python package x402-a2a 0.1.0, but no such package was found on PyPI.
The a2a-x402 repository published release v0.1.0 on 2025-09-16, the same day as Google's AP2 announcement.
The auth-capture EVM binding uses base/commerce-payments v1.1 AuthCaptureEscrow by default, with extra.operatorType of delegated or custom.
The x402 Foundation's working groups wg-identity, wg-tax, wg-card-acceptance and wg-domain-discovery exist as repositories; their outputs were not assessed.
Learning resources on x402 include a BetaKit podcast with Erik Reppel (2025-05-26), a Devconnect talk on x402scan by Merit Systems, and QuickNode tutorials on paywalls and Solana RPC.
